title: The reduction tower of an integral complex does not depend on the K-flat resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a scheme $Y$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with projections $\pi_n:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{E,n})_Y$, let $\rho_n:(A_{E,n+1})_Y\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the reduction maps, so that $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$, and let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived category of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]; let $\operatorname{Res}_n:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived restriction of scalars [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars].

Let $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, choose a complex representing it, also denoted $K$, and let $q:P\to K$ and $q':P'\to K$ be quasi-isomorphisms from K-flat complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $n\geq1$ put $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $P'_n=P'\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y$ (termwise change of rings along $\pi_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), read as complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules via $\pi_n$; let $\gamma_n:P\to P_n$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and $\tau_n=\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\rho_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ be the resulting morphisms of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules, and $\gamma'_n,\tau'_n$ the same for $P'$. Let $\theta_n:P_n\to P'_n$ be the canonical isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ between the two computations of the derived change of rings along $\pi_n$ given by the K-flat resolutions $q$ and $q'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, clause 2]. Then:

1. $\operatorname{Res}_n(\theta_n)\circ[\gamma_n]\circ[q]^{-1}=[\gamma'_n]\circ[q']^{-1}$ as morphisms $K\to\operatorname{Res}_n(P'_n)$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$;
2. $\operatorname{Res}_n(\theta_n)\circ[\tau_n]=[\tau'_n]\circ\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(\theta_{n+1})$ as morphisms $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(P_{n+1})\to\operatorname{Res}_n(P'_n)$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$.

So the inverse systems $(\operatorname{Res}_nP_n,[\tau_n])_n$ and $(\operatorname{Res}_nP'_n,[\tau'_n])_n$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, together with their maps from $K$, are isomorphic through $(\operatorname{Res}_n\theta_n)_n$.

proof.text: Write $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ and $B_n=(A_{E,n})_Y$. Work first in the homotopy category of $R$-module complexes. Apply the right-hand (MS2) assertion of [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated] to $q:P\to K$ and $q':P'\to K$: there are $t:V\to P'$ a quasi-isomorphism and $g:V\to P$ with $qg=q't$ in the homotopy category. Two-out-of-three from that same node makes $g$ a quasi-isomorphism. Choose a K-flat resolution $r:T\to V$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and put $a=gr:T\to P$, $b=tr:T\to P'$. Thus $a,b$ are quasi-isomorphisms, all three complexes $T,P,P'$ are K-flat, and $qa=q'b$ in the homotopy category. Choose chain representatives for $a,b$; no direct chain map from $P$ to $P'$ is assumed.

Let $F_n$ be termwise change of rings and put $T_n=F_n(T)$, $a_n=F_n(a)$, $b_n=F_n(b)$. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes $a_n,b_n$ quasi-isomorphisms. The published scalar-reduction witness [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] already supplies its universal derived pair $(L_n,\varepsilon_n)$ and invertible K-flat computations. Whisker the counit with the quotient comparison to express it naturally on complexes. Naturality gives $[a_n]\varepsilon_T=\varepsilon_P L_n([a])$ and $[b_n]\varepsilon_T=\varepsilon_{P\prime}L_n([b])$. The resolution computations are $c_q=\varepsilon_P L_n([q])^{-1}$ and $c_{q\prime}=\varepsilon_{P\prime}L_n([q\prime])^{-1}$, with $\theta_n=c_{q\prime}c_q^{-1}$. Substitute these formulas into naturality and use $[q][a]=[q\prime][b]$ to get $\theta_n[a_n]=[b_n]$. Apply exact derived restriction and use its canonical localization factorization [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars]. Naturality of that factorization transports the identity to the actual restricted complexes. All coefficient and site universes stay independent. The legacy finite-field interface uses the same coefficient projection and universal witness. Naturality of quotientCompQhIso on the resolution augmentation identifies the two resolution-isomorphism conventions, so the legacy complex and resolution computations now directly reuse the canonical unrestricted definitions; hence its finite and restricted comparisons coincide with the unrestricted comparisons.

Write $\gamma^T_n:T\to T_n$, $z\mapsto z\otimes1$. The tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $a_n\gamma^T_n=\gamma_n a$ and $b_n\gamma^T_n=\gamma'_n b$: both sides send a local section $z$ to $a(z)\otimes1$, respectively $b(z)\otimes1$; sheafifying these equalities and applying localization preserves them. Put $\alpha_n=\operatorname{Res}_n([a_n])$, $\beta_n=\operatorname{Res}_n([b_n])$. Then $\operatorname{Res}_n(\theta_n)=\beta_n\alpha_n^{-1}$. Because $[a]^{-1}[q]^{-1}=([q][a])^{-1}=([q'][b])^{-1}=[b]^{-1}[q']^{-1}$, we obtain $\beta_n\alpha_n^{-1}[\gamma_n][q]^{-1}=\beta_n[\gamma^T_n][a]^{-1}[q]^{-1}=[\gamma'_n][q']^{-1}$. This proves clause (1). Construct the chain unit directly from the normalized ordinary scalar-extension/restriction adjunction of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]. Its naturality gives these chain-map identities without unfolding the inverse-limit coefficient ring. The normalization proves unrestrictedTowerUnit_condition; uniqueness identifies the construction with the originally specified unit. For the legacy unit and transition existence-and-uniqueness statement, use the published unrestricted maps as witnesses. Units agree sectionwise. For transitions, transport the source by the defining tensor-object equality, forget to abelian sheaves, and apply sheafify_hom_ext; tensor induction reduces equality to the prescribed pure-tensor formula. Thus the selected legacy maps equal the unrestricted maps.

proof.text: Let $\tau^T_n=1_T\otimes\rho_n$. Pure-tensor functoriality [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $a_n\tau^T_n=\tau_n a_{n+1}$ and $b_n\tau^T_n=\tau'_n b_{n+1}$: on $z\otimes c$ the first two sides are $a(z)\otimes\rho_n(c)$, and the second two are $b(z)\otimes\rho_n(c)$. They are $R$-linear because $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$, commute with differentials, and remain equal after sheafification and localization. Thus $\alpha_n^{-1}[\tau_n]=[\tau^T_n]\alpha_{n+1}^{-1}$ and $\beta_n[\tau^T_n]=[\tau'_n]\beta_{n+1}$, so $\operatorname{Res}_n(\theta_n)[\tau_n]=\beta_n\alpha_n^{-1}[\tau_n]=[\tau'_n]\beta_{n+1}\alpha_{n+1}^{-1}=[\tau'_n]\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(\theta_{n+1})$. This proves clause (2). Each component is invertible, so these equations give the claimed tower isomorphism; rearranging them gives compatibility of the inverse components as well. The pre-localization unrestrictedIntegralTransition is already a natural transformation on complexes by its defining type, so apply its naturality to a and b, localize and cancel the reduced quasi-isomorphism a.
